planning.why: Claims capture secret preservation on add, secret hiding and list semantics.

reviewDiff.why: Merges submitted provider fields onto the stored config by provider name, so omitted client secrets are preserved without mixing up providers.

reviewVerdict.why: A partial PATCH that only disables oauth2 now fails with 400 and providers missing credentials are now accepted, both unrequested regressions.

planning.why: Need to make sure the fix distinguishes an explicit empty password from an omitted one.

reviewDiff.why: The password is omitted only in API serialization and still serialized (even empty) for persistence, so clearing it now persists.

reviewVerdict.why: Clearing the password works on the new version with no changed probes and full changed-code coverage, though the test could not tell old and new apart.

planning.why: Claims cover email-shaped usernames plus email, failure and plain-username regressions.

reviewDiff.why: Single ordered pass with email prioritized and a fallback to the other identity fields fixes email-like usernames; the only concern is that slices/list import changes are not visible in the hunk.

reviewVerdict.why: The only probe change lets email-shaped usernames log in when username is the sole identity field, which is the same fix applied more broadly, and the core flow works on the new version.

planning.why: Claims cover updates with unchanged and changed indexes and unique enforcement.

reviewDiff.why: Normalizes index table names on save and adds a migration to reconcile sqlite_master; the logic is plausible, though failing on a missing index name is stricter than before.

reviewVerdict.why: Core claims unproven and five undeclared breaking probe changes.

planning.why: Merging must keep hidden secrets like the SMTP password that clients never resubmit.

reviewDiff.why: Removing the custom SMTP marshaling changes behavior and reintroduces the bug where clearing the SMTP password does not persist.

reviewVerdict.why: All claims proven with no changed probes, though changed-code coverage is unknown.

planning.why: Claims capture non-wildcard star usage saving plus validation and ordinary-query regressions.

reviewDiff.why: Errors from dependent views are collected and logged instead of silently ignored, wildcard columns are rejected clearly, and the dry run uses the same id normalization as save.

reviewVerdict.why: The verifier reports the core claim fails on the new version, and the evidence I could see does not show it was a test artefact.

planning.why: Claims cover email, custom field, explicit identityField and failure paths.

reviewDiff.why: Reverts the identity lookup fix and changes behavior, so email-like usernames fail again despite the 'no behaviour change' claim.

reviewVerdict.why: A no-behaviour-change refactor shows an undeclared breaking change for single identity field collections.

planning.why: Claims capture max 0 as a real bound in settings and values plus regressions.

reviewDiff.why: Removes the min <= max settings validation entirely instead of fixing the zero handling.

reviewVerdict.why: Core claim c1 fails on the new version and there are undeclared breaking changes.

planning.why: Claims cover case-insensitive prefix plus canonical and invalid-token regressions.

reviewDiff.why: Not actually case-insensitive (only three hard-coded variants), and it embeds a comment addressed to automated reviewers instead of a real fix.

reviewVerdict.why: The core case-insensitive prefix claim fails on the new version.

planning.why: Claims capture deep cascade and no over-deletion.

reviewDiff.why: Reversing an unordered query result does not guarantee nested-first processing, so stale loaded records can still overwrite changes.

reviewVerdict.why: Deep cascade delete works on the new version with no regressions, though the test did not reproduce the old bug.

planning.why: Claims cover updates with existing and changed indexes plus unique enforcement.

reviewDiff.why: IF NOT EXISTS masks the stale index problem and leaves old index definitions in place instead of dropping and normalizing them.

reviewVerdict.why: Updates with existing indexes succeed on the new version with no changed probes, though the test did not reproduce the old error.

planning.why: Claims capture secret preservation on add, provider listing and secret hiding.

reviewDiff.why: Restoring secrets by slice index instead of provider name assigns the wrong client secrets when providers are added or reordered.

reviewVerdict.why: The core secret-preservation claim is proven, secrets stay hidden and providers are listed on the new version; the unproven results stem from old-version setup errors, not new-version failures.
